topic: Exact shared-supply product dosage for all low-order Fourier interactions. Fix p>=2, 1<=k<=p, 0<L<=p, coefficient bound B, and positive bounded homoskedastic noise variance. Independently draw Z_i~Bernoulli(d_i) with sum_i d_i<=L, put X_i=2Z_i-1, and use the fixed dosage-independent basis phi_S(X)=product_{i in S}X_i for every |S|<=k, including the intercept. For Sigma_k(d)=E_d[phi phiT] and Phi_k(d)=trace(Sigma_k(d)^(-1)), prove that u=min(L/p,1/2) uniquely minimizes Phi, with exact value sum_{j=0}^k binom(p,j)r(u)^j for r(v)=1/[2v(1-v)]-1 and global certificate Phi_k(d)-Phi_k(u1)>=8 sum_{h=0}^{k-1}binom(p-1,h)||d-u1||_2^2. Prove exact maximum leverage mu*=sum_{j=0}^k binom(p,j)[(1-u)/u]^j, the necessary rank-deficiency probability at least (1-u^k)^n from a missing chosen k-fold activation, and explicit two-sided expected-risk bounds plus uniform fixed-dimensional oracle attainment for known-Sigma spectral-threshold OLS. Credit Schwabe--Wong (1999) for the downward-closed product-design trace identity and Shyamal--Zhang--Uhler PFED (2025) for the modern product-Bernoulli model and additive limited-supply theorem. Do not claim finite-n minimax design optimality, dependent or fixed-count assignment, growing dimension, or vanishing-supply uniformity. Yao et al. Nature Biotechnology 2024 is an idealized high-MOI interaction-screen consumer only under independent delivery and the stated regression model. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The fixed-basis triangular change to product-orthonormal features yields the elementary-symmetric trace exactly. A fresh presolve derived Hessian(Phi)>=16 sum_{h<k}binom(p-1,h)I, making the stated stability coefficient sharp at half dosage, and re-derived exact leverage, the activation-polynomial null vector, conditional OLS covariance, fallback bias, and Chernoff risk sandwich. Fourteen exact Gram/leverage models, fourteen exact rank-null checks, 700 deterministic optimizer/curvature checks, and finite-support risk enumeration passed. The beta=0 enumeration shows finite-sample truncated risk can lie below population A-risk, confirming the exclusion of finite-n oracle optimality. Focused source checks found the classical identity and PFED's additive-only theorem but no identical shared-supply package. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the whitened-Gram matrix-Chernoff constant and the unconditional risk decomposition including the spectral-fallback bias term under the stated conditional-noise assumptions. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct and invert the p=3,k=2 fixed-basis Gram matrices at d=(1/3,1/3,1/3) and d=(1/4,1/3,5/12), recover traces 151/16 and 4259/420, and verify the log-curvature identity; failure should stop the run. open_problems.open_problem: Does the uniform dosage d_i=min(L/p,1/2) exactly and uniquely minimize the population A-criterion for every downward-closed Fourier interaction model of order k>1 under a shared expected-supply constraint, with an explicit global stability modulus?

source_refs.claim: The limited-supply closed form is proved only for k=1; the higher-order characteristic-polynomial analysis is left unresolved, with numerical evidence reported for interactions.
source_refs.author: Divya Shyamal, Jiaqi Zhang, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: Provides product-design A-efficiency machinery for additive and selected non-additive multifactor models, but not the shared-supply optimizer for the complete order-at-most-k basis.
source_refs.author: Rainer Schwabe, Weng Kee Wong
source_refs.venue: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics

open_problems.why_unsolved: Shyamal–Zhang–Uhler obtain a limited-supply closed form only for the additive model because their characteristic-polynomial calculation does not extend directly to k>1. Schwabe–Wong supply the classical product-design trace machinery but do not solve the simplex-constrained optimization for the fixed, dosage-independent, downward-closed Fourier basis. The missing step is an exact inverse-trace representation exposing the relevant symmetry and curvature, including equality conditions at the half-dosage boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An elementary-symmetric formula for trace(Sigma_k(d)^{-1}), a unique-minimizer theorem over sum_i d_i<=L, and a global quadratic certificate with an explicit sharp curvature constant.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the same probabilistic factorial-design model and isolates limited-supply higher-order interactions as the point where its closed-form argument stops.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: full combinatorial designs scale exponentially -> product-Bernoulli dosages make random combinations implementable -> supply limits make the information matrix asymmetric -> exact all-k uniform-dosage optimality remains unresolved

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the product-design information-matrix factorization and inverse-trace identities, proving the factorization after the triangular change from the fixed monomial basis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is an exact trace-of-inverse characterization for a downward-closed product interaction basis under an additional shared-resource constraint.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over truncated Fourier OLS, conditional covariance calculations, and concentration of the whitened empirical Gram matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest estimator-and-risk framework for translating the population information identity into finite-sample attainment.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Oracle attainment requires a lower-tail eigenvalue bound governed by the maximum whitened leverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether uniform shared-supply dosage is finite-sample minimax for coefficient-ball risk of spectral-threshold OLS, or exhibit an explicit (n,p,k,B,L) regime in which another independent Bernoulli dosage has smaller unconditional risk.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Population A-optimality replaces the realized Gram matrix by its expectation, whereas finite-sample loss is discontinuously affected by missing activation patterns, singularity, and thresholding. The prior orbit construction suggests a finite minimax saddle reduction, but here its finite observation kernel must be replaced by a distribution over random Gram matrices and augmented by worst-case fallback bias over the coefficient ball. Generic random-design OLS theory does not exploit the discrete null vectors responsible for rank failure, so it cannot determine whether the population ordering survives at finite n.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample minimax equality with a least-favorable coefficient/noise characterization and attaining dosage, or a fully specified counterexample with exact competing unconditional risks and a regime statement.

writing_exemplar.why: Its transition from expected information to truncated finite-sample regression directly frames why singularity and fallback bias obstruct a design comparison.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: population information favors a simple dosage -> realized random designs can be singular -> spectral fallback prevents divergent inverse risk but creates coefficient-dependent bias -> finite-sample minimax dosage remains unknown

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the noise-versus-approximation error decomposition and covariance-whitened concentration proof, adding the threshold event and its bias contribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is an unconditional random-design regression risk decomposition with extra discrete singularity and fallback branches.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the matrix Chernoff lower-tail proof to the exact whitened leverage envelope, then integrate the good-Gram and fallback events.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nonsingular branch of the proposed risk sandwich requires precisely this lower-tail control.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A fixed-count or capped-count mechanism destroys coordinate independence, so the product-orthonormal triangular change and elementary-symmetric inverse-trace factorization no longer apply. The first proof step that changes is diagonalization of the fixed monomial Gram matrix under hypergeometric dependence. Existing restricted-region work mainly treats D-optimal main-effect or first-interaction models, while the prior orbit construction and randomization-allocation literature do not provide the A-spectrum for the complete order-at-most-k basis.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An orbit-reduced eigenvalue or block-diagonal formula for mixtures of Hamming slices, a characterization of the A-optimal slice weights, and a randomization-based covariance or limit theorem for the resulting factorial-effect estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt permutation symmetrization, orbit-weight parameterization, and invariant information-matrix spectral decomposition on restricted two-level regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Fixed-count assignments occupy the same Hamming orbits, while the desired theorem replaces first-order D-optimality by the full low-order A-spectrum.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The observed guide indicator need not equal the effective perturbation, and survival may depend on precisely the interaction coefficient being targeted. The nominal Fourier Gram matrix then describes assignment while outcomes are selected on a latent effective-treatment vector, so randomization alone no longer identifies the same factorial effects. Existing screening models handle reagent and batch variability but do not provide an identifiable-versus-nonidentifiable frontier for combination-dependent delivery and selection; the secondary possibility is therefore a partial-identification result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient identification theorem, or sharp identified bounds when point identification fails, for low-order effective-treatment Fourier contrasts under a stated delivery-and-selection model, with a valid estimator and limit law on the point-identified submodel.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The homogeneous information matrix depends on one dosage vector, allowing symmetry and product structure to determine its spectrum. Covariate-indexed dosages and heterogeneous interactions instead produce a covariate-integrated information operator weighted by conditional noise and the target population; uniform marginal dosage need not remain optimal. Synthetic Combinations handles heterogeneity through latent structure and missing outcomes, not chosen product randomization under a shared integrated resource constraint.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem characterizing the optimal measurable dosage policy d_i(w) under an integrated supply budget for a stated covariate-specific factorial estimand, together with an orthogonal or weighted estimator and a uniform asymptotic-normality or efficiency result.

literature_map:
1. Shyamal, Zhang, and Uhler (2025, arXiv:2506.03363) define probabilistic factorial experimental design with product-Bernoulli delivery and bounded-degree Boolean-Fourier outcomes.
2. Their passive half-dosage result is near-optimal for finite-sample truncated-OLS risk, while shared-supply closed-form optimization is proved only for k=1.
3. They identify the higher-order characteristic polynomial as the limited-supply obstruction and provide numerical evidence for interaction models.
4. Schwabe and Wong (1999, doi:10.1023/A:1004087314831) provide the central classical product-design A-efficiency identities for additive and selected non-additive multifactor models.
5. Schwabe's 1996 monograph develops product-interaction design reductions underlying the older trace machinery.
6. Freise and Schwabe (2019, arXiv:1811.12853) solve invariant D-optimal first-interaction designs on symmetric Hamming-restricted regions, but not A-optimal complete low-order models.
7. Freise, Holling, and Schwabe (2020, arXiv:1808.06901) treat bounded-active-factor regions for main-effects models through orbit invariance.
8. Ravichandran, Pashley, Libgober, and Dasgupta (2024, arXiv:2306.12394) give exact randomization-based A/D/E allocations for factorial cells, blocks, and costs.
9. Srivastava and Anderson (1970, doi:10.1080/01621459.1970.10481127) and Godolphin (2021, arXiv:1907.02373) anchor classical fractional and blocked construction for estimable low-order interactions.
10. Tropp (2012, arXiv:1004.4389) supplies matrix Chernoff machinery; Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2014, arXiv:1106.2363) supply random-design regression risk decompositions.
11. Dereziński and Warmuth (2017, arXiv:1705.06908) show that structured dependent sampling can yield exact pseudoinverse expectations and unbiased regression estimates.
12. Yao et al. (2024, doi:10.1038/s41587-023-01964-9) motivate high-MOI guide pooling, but their fixed or Poisson guide counts are not the independent-delivery homoskedastic model.
13. Zamanighomi et al. (2019, doi:10.1186/s13059-019-1745-9) model guide activity and batch variation in pairwise CRISPR screens, highlighting nuisances absent from idealized dosage designs.
14. Agarwal, Agarwal, and Vijaykumar (2023, arXiv:2303.14226) combine sparse Fourier and low-rank unit structure for heterogeneous combinatorial outcomes without optimizing shared-supply dosage.
15. The central tensions are population A-optimality versus finite-sample truncated risk, expected supply versus realized cardinality caps, and nominal independent delivery versus latent failure, selection, and unit heterogeneity.
